subject: Clarifying what Redwood stores by default (requests, prompts, outputs) & opt-out paths
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Verma <sasha.verma@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify default data storage for requests/outputs

Hi Karthik,

We're kicking off a short eval of Redwood for an internal healthcare analytics pipeline and need a clear, plain-language answer on what Redwood stores by default when using the hosted API: specifically

- Are full request payloads (prompts) retained?
- Are model-generated outputs retained separately from requests?
- What's the default retention window for each (requests, responses, metadata/telemetry)?
- Where are those logs stored (region/residency)?

We have to feed this into our security review checklist — if you can point to the Console toggle or API to opt-out of storage that would be ideal. I've attached a quick matrix of the data categories we're tracking.

Thanks,
Liam
Director of Platform Security
Acme Analytics

Attachment: retention-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify default data storage for requests/outputs

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list, and welcome. Short answer up front: for Hosted accounts, Redwood retains request/response logs by default for troubleshooting and SLO analysis, but there are documented opt-out controls and a documented purge path. Longer details and exact windows below. Looping in Neha (security) and Marissa (product) for precision + regional residency notes.

I'll summarize the default policy then call out opt-outs and deletion paths. If you'd rather do a quick call I can have our compliance engineer join.

— Karthik
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

Reference link: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/security/retention

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify default data storage for requests/outputs

Hi Liam — adding the specifics you can use in your security checklist. I'll keep this focused and practical.

Default (Hosted API) — how we treat each category by default: 
- Request payloads (prompts): retained as part of the request log. Default retention: 30 days. Treated as customer-provided data.
- Model outputs (generated text): retained alongside request logs and tagged as "generated_output". Default retention: 30 days.
- Metadata/telemetry (latency, token counts, route, model version): retained for 90 days for analytics and SLOs; aggregated/yearly rollups kept longer in anonymized form.
- KV cache and runtime-only caches: in-memory or ephemeral on GPU hosts. Not persisted to long-term object storage by default.

Residency: logs for Hosted customers are stored in the region configured on the account (e.g., us-west-2 or eu-west-1). If you sign up in the US region, logs do not leave the US region for storage. We can provide region-specific export statements for SOC/compliance reviews.

Opt-out & purge paths: 
- Console toggle: Account > Data Controls > "Disable request/response retention" — when enabled, Redwood will stop persisting full request/response payloads to long-term storage for new requests.
- Per-request header: x-redwood-no-store: true — we honor this for hosted customers; requests with that header are processed but not persisted.
- On-demand purge: Customers can open a deletion request via the Console or the Data Deletion API (POST /v1/admin/data/purge) — we will schedule a targeted purge and provide an audit log. Purge request SLA: 72 hours.

Backups & snapshots: Hosted system backups of model-serving infra are encrypted and retained for 7 days; backups do not include long-term request logs unless retention was enabled.

Exceptions: Some minimal telemetry required for abuse detection and platform health is retained short-term even when retention is disabled; this is documented and minimized.

Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope summary)

Let me know if you need a Board-ready paragraph and I'll draft one.
— Neha
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify default data storage for requests/outputs

Thanks Neha — that helps a lot. Two quick follow-ups:
1) If we enable the Console toggle to disable retention, can you confirm the on-disk copies are deleted immediately for previously retained requests, or only upon a manual purge request?
2) Our pipeline stores some PII in prompts occasionally (names/IDs). If we request a purge, will Redwood also remove any derived artifacts (e.g., cached KV fragments, prompt-based augmentations) or just the logs/objects?

We're sensitive to the 72-hour purge SLA but need clarity on what exactly is removed so we can scope our internal de-identification.

— Liam

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify default data storage for requests/outputs

Hi Liam — quick clarifications to both bullets: 

1) Console toggle vs historical data: Enabling the "Disable request/response retention" toggle prevents new request/response payloads from being written to long-term storage. It does NOT automatically delete historical preserved logs. For historical data we run an on-demand purge when requested (Console UI or Data Deletion API). We will provide an audit entry once the purge is complete.

2) Scope of purge: The purge process targets all persisted artifacts related to the specified account or request IDs, including: 
   - request/response logs in object storage;
   - generated_output objects that were stored;
   - index references used by internal tooling for that account (search/index metadata).

What we do NOT typically purge (and why):
   - aggregated/anonymous telemetry used for SLOs where the data is irreversibly aggregated;
   - backups/snapshots that cannot be retroactively modified; per our backup policy these are short-lived (7d) and encrypted; we exclude the long-term logs from snapshots where retention is disabled.

KV caches and runtime-only artifacts: those are not written to long-term stores and are therefore not part of purges — they are ephemeral and cleared per-host lifecycle. If your workflow uses Redwood Dedicated/Private and you have local indexes we can provide a runbook to purge those as well (Private/Dedicated give you full control).

Next steps I propose:
- We can run a targeted purge for a small set of request IDs you provide so you can validate removal and audit entries.
- I'll have Marissa send you the customer-facing paragraph for your security packet.

Would you like to schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to run through the deletion API and provide sample purge request logs?

— Karthik
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference
